title: Singleton coefficient and discrete derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f:\{ -1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. The biased Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $\{i\}$ equals $\sigma_p$ times the product-distribution mean of its discrete derivative in coordinate $i$, where $\sigma_p=\sqrt{4p(1-p)}$ and the discrete derivative is half the difference between the values with that coordinate set to $1$ and to $-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$i$ is a coordinate in the $n$-dimensional cube
